children.value: This page was migrated from the CHM 696 course materials developed by Jonathan Hood and Lyudmila Slipchenko. Equations and examples remain under editorial review during the Fall 2026 website migration.
By the end of this lecture, you should be able to:
classify a second-order linear PDE from its principal part;

distinguish the propagation behavior of elliptic, hyperbolic, parabolic, and
dispersive equations;
solve rectangular-domain problems by separation of variables; and
use Fourier or Laplace transforms to reduce a linear PDE to ODEs.
